decision_changed: A recovering site adds a scope-taking operator to the corpus and, since this is authored against canonical control v2, its C enters the comparable set directly. A capability stop with the not-only side failing would be the second instance of a frame default beating an explicit cue, which would make that a general property worth stating rather than a one-off.
novelty_delta: Sixteenth behaviour. Prior-art search returns 0 events for not only, additive, scope and but. The nearest existing behaviour is correlative_state.either_vs_neither: both are paired connectives, but that one is a DISJUNCTION choice where the first element selects between two continuations, whereas here a focus particle takes scope over a whole clause and obliges a contrastive continuation, against a plain adverb that leaves the default coordinator. Recipient and donor differ only in that adverb position and end on the same noun token; A2 re-expresses it in a report frame. RISK RECORDED BEFORE THE RUN: the countability null measured an hour earlier showed that a verb frame's default continuation can override a cue entirely (" much" after a negated verb, " many" after "collected"). Here " and" is the default after a direct object, so this screen is a test of whether an explicit scope operator is strong enough to beat a frame default; a capability stop on the not-only side would be that same finding again rather than a stimulus defect.
